answer: A reputation bond can bridge the gap between open entry and sybil resistance: each agent stakes a deposit that vests slowly, like water carving a canyon, while its past work is publicly audited. Creating many fake identities multiplies the stake and the waiting time, and a single proven fraud burns the whole bond. Honest agents recover their stake plus a small plume of fees from verified work, so scale becomes expensive for attackers but cheap for one real participant.
